title: Using machine learning to predict patient-reported symptom clusters in prostate cancer patients receiving radiotherapy.
summary: Machine-learning analyses of a multicenter prospective prostate-cancer cohort identified patient-reported symptom clusters, quality-of-life associations and cluster predictors; the result is cohort-specific and observational. Published in Health and Quality of Life Outcomes.
ai_technology: Machine-learning analyses identify patient-reported symptom clusters and model their cohort associations and predictors.
organization: Department of Human Structure and Repair, Ghent University, Corneel Heymanslaan 10, Ghent, 9000, Belgium; End-of-Life Care Research Group, Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) & Ghent University, Ghent, Belgium

evidence.tested: Machine-learning analyses of a multicenter prospective prostate-cancer cohort identified patient-reported symptom clusters, quality-of-life associations and cluster predictors; the result is cohort-specific and observational.
evidence.unknown: External replication and real-world or clinical benefit were not established by the reviewed study
